Ārya_(?)
--C. on Kaṁsavadhanāṭaka of Śeṣakṛṣṇa. BORI. 13 of 1874-75. BORI. D. XIV. 44 (TIkAryanAmnA padakaumudI-).

Ārya,_Āryapa
another form of the name of Appayārya (Jinendrakalyāṇābhyudaya otherwise called Vidyānuvāsāṅga). Praśasti Saṁgraha p.. 10, 11, 12.

Āryaka
a name of the poet Ghanaśyāma of Tanjore Mahratta Court. See his Damaruka, MD. 12519 (col.). (edn. Śaṅkara Gurukula Patrikā, I. 1939-40).

Āryacandra
Bud. Vaibhāṣika.
--Maitreyavyākaraṇa or Maitreyasamiti.
On the prophecy about Maitreya; frequently transl. into Chinese, Central Asian languages an. Tibetan. Chinese versions, A. D. 255-316, C. 402 an. 701. RASB. I. (p. 13f). a.'s name found in Tokharian an. Uigurian frags.
See Sitzungsberichte der Preussischen Akadamie der Wissenschaften in Berlin, 1916, p.. 396, 491f an. E. Leumann, Maitreyasamiti, Strassburg 1919, Tokharian or North Aryan version.

Āryatulya
jy. by Duh2khabhañjana. Oudh VIII. 14.

Āryadāsa
--Kalpāgamasaṅgrahavādhūlakalpasūtravyākhyā. Adyar. MT. 2978. Trav. Uni. L. 123A. L. 124.

Āryadeva
or deva Bud. A. D. 200-225. known also a. Nīlanetra an. Kāṇadeva. Came from South India or Ceylon (see IHQ. IX. p.. 978-9; X. p.. 137-42, 368-373, on his home); pupil of Nāgārjuna. A legendary [Page168-a. life of his transl. into Chinese by Kumārajīva (A.D. 401-9), Nanjio 1462. See also Ind. Ant. IV. p. 142. See Intro. p. xv. to Cittaviśuddhiprakaraṇa, Viśvabhāratī Studies 8, for two Āryadevas, the Catuśśataka etc. being works of the earlier one, Cittaviśuddhi etc. of a later one.
--Akṣaraśataka. See NCC. I. p. 11b.
--Atiguhyācintyanāma pañcaviṣaguptamārga. Cordier II. p. 250.
--Abhisambodhikramopadeśa. Cordier II. p. 136. JBORS. XXIII. i. p. 38 (no. 256).
--Krodhabhayanāśanīsamayaguhyasādhana. Cordier III. p. 225.
--Krodhabhayanāśanīsādhana. Cordier III. p. 225.
--Krodhabhayanāśinīhomavidhi. Cordier III. p. 226.
--Guhyasamājaniṣpannakramāntaka. Cordier II. p. 137.
--Catuh2pīṭhagūḍhārthanirdeśa Ekadruma pañjikā. Cordier II. p.. 99-100.
--Catuh2pīṭhatantrarājamaṇḍalopāyikāvidhisārasamuccayanāma. Cordier II. p. 99.
--Catuh2pīṭhayogatantrasādhanopāyikā. Cordier II. p. 99.

Viśvabhāratī Series 2, 1931; P. L. Vaidya, Etudes sur Āryadeva et son Catuśśataka, Paris 1923; see also Tucci, Rivista degli studi orientali, Rome, X, 1923, 521 ff.
--Caryāmelāyanapradīpa. Cordier II. p. 136. [Page168-b]
--Cittaviśuddhi (Cittāvaraṇaviśodhananāma or Cittaratnaviśodhana prakaraṇa or simply Cittaprakaraṇa). Cordier II. p. 136. III. p. 232. Nepal II. p. 249.
Pt.. JASB. 1898; also separately, Viśvabhāratī Studies 8, 1949. See also BSOS. London, VI. p.. 411 ff. Owing to later Tāntrik ideas an. references to Rāśis etc., this has been taken to be a later work an. not a work of the early Āryadeva.
--Jñānasārasamuccaya. Cordier III. p. 298. JBORS. XXI. p. 30.
--Jñāneśvarīsādhana. Cordier II. p. 99.

--Nirvikalpakaprakaraṇa. Bud. Cordier II. p. 223.
--Nairātmāpañcadaśadevīstotra. Cordier III. p. 128.
--Pañcakrama. Bud. JBORS. XXIII. i. p. 38.
--Prajñāpāramitāmahāparipṛcchā. Cordier III. p. 497.
--Prajñāpradīpaśāstrakārikā(vyākhyā). Nanjio 1185.

--Bhagavanmañjughoṣavicāraṇa. Cordier II. p. 299.

--Madhyamakabhramaghātanāma. Cordier III. p. 298.
--Mahādevatrayasādhana. Cordier III. p. 226.
--Mahāpuruṣaśāstra. Nanjio 1242.

--Vajraghaṇṭapūjāsādhanakrama. Cordier II. p. 100.
--Śataśāstra. Nanjio 1188 (with C. by Vasubandhu). Text transl. into English, Tucci, GOS. XLIX.
--Śataśāstravaipulya. Nanjio 1189. 1198 (with C. by Dharmapāla).
--[Śatākṣaraśāstra. Nanjio 1254. See Akṣaraśataka].

--Hastabala(-bāla-)prakaraṇa or Muṣṭiprakaraṇa in 6 verses; a. epitome of the illusoriness of phenomena an. the two kinds of reality. Cordier III. p.. 297-8 (text an. C.). Nanjio 1255. 1256 (wrongly ascribed to Jina). JASB. 1908. p.. 375-6 (Hastabala). Skt. text reconstructed from Chinese an. Tibetan, F. W. Thomas an. Ui, JRAS. 1918, 267 ff.
--Hevajraḍākinījālamahātantraṭīkā, Vajraratnāvalī. JBORS. XXI. i. p. 38 (no. 118). Col. however mentions Līlāvajra a. a. [Page169-b]
--‘Śāstra on the regulation of the principles of the four heretical Hīnayāna schools mentioned in the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra.’ Nanjio 1259. (Bodhiruci's Chin. transl. A. D. 508-535).
--‘Śāstra on the explanation of the Nirvāṇa of twenty heretical Hīnayāna teachers mentioned in the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra.’ Nanjio 1260. (Bodhiruci's Chin. Transl. A. D. 508-535).
One an. half verses of Āryadeva cited in Maitreyanātha's Bhavasaṅkrānti Ṭīkā, Adyar edn. p. 34, are not found in an. ptd. work of Āryadeva.

Āryadeva
Poet. Sbhv. 1750.

Āryadeva
a Jain teacher eulogised in IO. 7606.

Āryadeva
Jain. Dig., successor of Varadatta, successor of Śivakoṭi.
--Tattvārthasūtra. See Epi. Car. VIII. Intro. p. 8, text p. 255; also ibid. II. Intro. p. 83. text p. 25, penultimate line.

Āryadeśasudhākara(ºraṇa)
nāṭaka. by Bhaṭṭavināyaka Nārāyaṇa Jyotirvid. Bombay, 1889. See IO. Pt.. Bk.. 1897, p. 14.

Āryadvādaśaka
stotra. Trav. Uni. 3605D. 12168H.

Āryādvādaśaka
stotra on Sūrya. MD. 11312. 17509. 17510. Sūryadvādaśāryāstotra.

Āryadharma
Bud. See ‘Report on the Gilgit excavation in 1938’, J. Myth. Soc. XXX. p. 7, a. inc. ms. in Gilgit.

Āryadharma
Jain teacher. Guerinot p. 377.

Āryadharmanīti
by Īśānacandravasu. Moral stanzas compiled from Manu, the epics, Viṣṇupurāṇa, Hitopadeśa etc. IInd Ed.. with Gujarati translation, Ahmadabad, 1895. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1892-1906. 235.

Āryadharmaprakāśikā
a. outline of Hindu religion an. philosophy for Hindu schools, by Maṇḍikal Rāma Śāstrī. [Page170-a.
Pt.. Mysore, 1890. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1892-1906. 547.

Āryadharmabodhinī
Hindu religious instructor by R. Sivasankara Pandyaji, Madras 1897. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1892-1906. 652.

Āryadharmaviveka
a modern philosophical tract by Tārakacandracūḍāmaṇi, with Beng. interpretation.
Pt.. (1) Medinipur, 1859 (Pt. I). (2) Calcutta, 1882 (Pt. II). See IO. Pt.. Bk.. 1897, p. 14; Ibid. 1938, p. 171.

Āryadhyāpitamuṣṭisūtra_(?)
Bud. Q. in Candrakīrti's Madhyamakavṛtti, Cambr. Uni. Bud. p. 116.

Āryanandi
Jain. C. 750 A. D. a teacher of the Pañcastūpānvaya to which Jinasena an. Guṇabhadra belonged; pupil of Candrasena an. preceptor of Vīrasena (Dhavalā on Ṣaṭkhaṇḍāgama). See Jain Ant. XII. i. p.. 1-6; N. Premi, Jain Sāh. aur Itihās, p.. 421, 498.

Āryanandiguru
Asaga wrote his Vardhamānacaritra a. the instance of this teacher. Peters. IV. 163.

Āryanandila
(Ajjanandila). Jain.
--Vairuṭyā (Vajroṣṭhī) stotra, Pkt. Jainagranthāvalī p. 291. Peters. III. Extr. p. 329; IV, Index of a.s. p. xi. See also Weber HIL. II. p.. 674, 919. For his story, see Prabhāvakacarita, story 3; śl. 80 here mentions the opening words of his Vairuṭyāstotra.

Āryaniyamodayakāvya
Āryasamāj. by Akhilānandaśarman.
Pt.. Meerut 1907. Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1906-28. 32-33.

Āryanītimatabodhinī
on moral conduct; ed. an. compiled by Śivaśaṅkara Pāṇḍya. The [Page170-b] Hindu Excelsior Series 1, Madras 1891. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1876-92. 391.

Āryapakṣagrahadīpa
jy. B. IV. 116.

Āryapañcamahāyajñapaddhati
Pt.. Ārṣagranthāvalī, Vol. VI. No. 7, Lahore, 1910. See IO. Pt.. Bk.. 1938, p. 173.

Āryapañjara
stotra. Trav. Uni. 5790 Z-20.

Āryapārya
Jain. a form of the correct name Appayārya, a. of Jinendrakalyāṇābhyudaya.

Āryabhaṭa
poet. Q. Kavikaṇṭhābharaṇa II an. in Sbhv. 1657.

Āryabhaṭa
I. jy. of Kusumapura; born A. D. 476; wrote in 499.
--Āryabhaṭīya. jy. Comprising the Daśagītikāsūtra (10-13 āryās) on numerical notation an. the Āryāṣṭaśata (108 āryās) in 3 pādas: gaṇita, kālakriyā an. gola. Some mss. an. commentators take the two parts a. two separate works. Probably wrote another, a Karaṇa work, dated 505 A.D., which has not yet come to light, but the substance of which is contained in the Khaṇḍakhādya of Brahmagupta. See Dikshit, Ind. Ant. XIX. p.. 45-54; Bhāratīya Jyotiṣa, p. 273, Hindi version; Sengupta, Dept. of Letters, Cal. Uni., XVIII. p.. 2-3 of his paper; On Āryabhaṭa I an. II an. their works, see Bull. Cal. Math. Soc. XVII. 1926, p.. 59-74; XVIII. 1927. p.. 5-18.

Āryabhaṭṭa
of Gārgya gotra; of Uttaramerūr, but living a. the Agrahāra, near Indugrāma; proficient in Dharmaśāstra; father of Śvetavanavāsin (Uṇādisūtravṛtti, Adyar D. VI. p. 125, MT. 4355, 5279. Ed.. Madras University Skt. Ser. VII. i. p. 57).

Āryabhaṭa_(?)
--Siddhāntamuktāvali (?) Oppert II. 6502.

Āryabhaṭakṛtasūtrārtha_(?)
jy. Sakti 39.

Āryabhaṭatantragaṇita
by Kodaṇḍarāma. MT. 371 (o). See below under C.s on Āryabhaṭīya.

Āryabhaṭatulyakaraṇagrantha
See under Bhaṭatulyakaraṇagrantha. [Page171-a.

Āryabhaṭavāṇī
adv. by Kodaṇḍarāma of Koṭikulapūḍi family. MT. 2156 (a.. This is a fourth supplementary chapter in verses to the author's C. on the three pādas of Āryabhaṭa's jy. work; this supplement deals with Advaitavedānta. See MT. 371 (o) for his C. on the Kālakriyāpāda of the Āryabhaṭīya.

Āryabhaṭasiddhānta
(or A. si.) jy. not known if Laghu of Ār. I or Mahat of Ār. II. Adyar II. p. 48a (2 mss.). Allahabad 180 (33). BORI. 104 (ii) of 1866-68. Gough p. 64. IL. 140 (Gola ch. only). 165. IM. 5117. Kavīndrācārya 855. Mandlik BL. 7. 11. NW. 522.
--C. by Raghunātha. Adyar. Śṛṅgeri 166.

Āryabhaṭīya
or Āryabhaṭatantra or Āryasiddhānta or Vṛddhāryasiddhānta or Laghvāryasiddhānta. by Āryabhaṭa I. Comprises the Daśagītikāsūtra an. Āryāṣṭaśata in 3 pādas. According to some mss. an. C.s, the two parts are considered a. two separate works an. the name Āryabhaṭīya is applied to the first or the second or to the whole. Edn.. Āryabhaṭīyaviṣayānukramaṇikā
jy. Adyar II. p. 48a.

Āryabhāṣya_(?)
name of a C. on the Sāṅkhyapravacanasūtras ascribed to Gauḍapāda. America 3567.

Āryamaṅgu(ºṅkṣu)
Jain. mentioned in Nandisūtra, Śrutāvatāra etc.
--C. on Kaṣāyaprābhṛta of Guṇadhara. N. Premi, Jain Sāh. aur Itihās p.. 6-8, 13, 539.

Āryamati
Bud.
--Ucchuṣmajambhālasādhana. Cordier III. p. 89.

Āryamahāgiri
Jain. brother of Āryasuhastin; pupil of Sthūlabhadrasvāmin; guru of Aśvamitra; See IO. Keith p. 1275b. Peters. III. App. p. 177. IV. Index p. XI. 94. V. 121, 139. [Page173-a.

Āryarakṣita
Jain. founder of Añcala or Vidhipakṣagaccha; predecessor of Jayasiṁhasūri, Bhuvanatuṅgasūri etc.; guru of Dharmaghoṣa (Śatapadikā, 1207 A. D.). Called Goḍu by father, Vijayacandra by teacher, an. Āryarakṣita a. Sūri. See BORI. D. XVII. i. (a. 291, 318; Peters. I. Intro. p. 63; III. App. p. 219 (Tīrthamālāstavana, 1st verse); IV. Index of a.s. p. xii, App. p. 115; V. App. p. 139; Praśasti I. p. 53. Ind. Ant. XXIII. p. 175.

Āryarakṣita
Jain. For others of that name see IO. 7639, Weber 1980, among Tapāgaccha teachers; ordained Bhadraguptācārya.

Āryarakṣita
a Śaibya introduced a. a character in the Bhāṇa, Pādatāḍitaka of Śyāmilaka. Caturbhāṇī edn. p. 7.

Āryarakṣitakathā
Jain. See C.. X. C. 55. Sūcīpattra 119 (Āryarakṣaṭakathā).

Āryarakṣitasūri
Jain. of Kharataragaccha; son of Somadeva; ref. to in Jain literature a. one who knew nine of the Pūrvas; his story told in Āvaśyakacūrṇī (p.. I. p.. 397-415); said to have passed away in Vīra saṁ. 584 or 597. See Ind. Ant. XI. p. 247; Peters. III. App. p. 308; Kapadia, Can. Lit. of the Jainas, p.. 52-53, 73. For his story, see Prabhāvakacarita, story no. 2. The supposition that Anuyogadvārasūtra is his work is wrong. See Kapadia, ibid. p. 161.

Āryavajra
Grammarian, q. in Abhinavaśākaṭāyana's Śabdānuśāsana, I. ii. 13, 14; vii. 2, 101. See also Ind. Ant. 1887. p.. 27. 28.

Āryavidyāsudhākara
compendium by Yajñeśvara Cimana Bhaṭṭa (1866).
Pt.. (1) Bombay 1868. (2) Lahore 1923. [Page173-b]

Āryavṛttenducandrikā_Savyākhyā
Āryasamāj. by Akhilānandaśarman.
Pt.. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1906-28. 32-33.

Āryaśaktistotra
Jain. Taylor I. 377.

Āryaśarman
of Kerala, father of Nārāyaṇa an. grandfather of Āryaśarman (Sadācāravṛttivartana MT. 4184), noted below.

Āryaśarman
famous doctor of Planthol House on the banks of the Bālā in Kerala; son of Nārāyaṇa an. grandson of Vaidya Āryaśarman an. student of his maternal uncle's son.
--Sadācāravṛttivartana, a treatise on a pure, healthy spiritual life. MT. 4184.

Āryaśirobhūṣaṇakāvya
Āryasamāj. by Akhilānandaśarman. Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1906-28. 32-33.

Āryaśūra
Bud. 4th cent. A. D. (?). Verses of his are found in Ajanta frescos (6th cent.) an. a work of his was transl. into Chinese in 434 A. D.
--Jātakamālā. Ed.. HOS. I.
